patterns.definition: A capability requirement is satisfied using a schema, interface, placeholder, fallback, metadata declaration, or test double rather than actual execution of the required capability.
examples: LLMExtractionTemplate treated as LLM_BACKED_EXTRACTION
FTS OR-query fallback treated as SEMANTIC_RETRIEVAL
Reviewer role schema treated as MULTIMODAL_REVIEW
Embedding candidate metadata treated as EMBEDDING_BENCHMARK
HybridRetriever class definition treated as HYBRID_RETRIEVAL

patterns.definition: A test proves that the implementation has the structure the builder just created but does not establish the professional or behavioral requirement that motivated that structure.
examples: hasattr(reviewer, "roles") == true does NOT prove visual reviewer correctly understands images
hybrid_search returns list does NOT prove retrieval is semantically meaningful
ExtractorVerifier.verify() returns dict does NOT prove independent verification
correct_pattern: Golden tasks must measure BEHAVIOR, TRUTH, QUALITY, FAILURE RESISTANCE
Not: API PRESENCE, STRUCTURE EXISTENCE, JSON PARSE SUCCESS

patterns.definition: The acceptance ledger marks tasks as COMPLETE while their own evidence remains NOT_RUN, incomplete, or not fresh. Acceptance is declared before all required primary-evidence gates have actually executed.
examples: Visual grounding V2 marked complete but no benchmark was run
Global deployment marked complete but hash proof was not executed
Acceptance matrix shows PASS while final report shows NOT_RUN
TODO ledger says done but evidence artifact does not exist
patterns.discovered_in: M002.1 Completion Pass 04 Final Truth-Closure Addendum

patterns.definition: A visual benchmark appears diverse because it contains many images while its ground-truth labels are substantially identical, allowing constant predictions to score highly without proving visual discrimination.
A benchmark accepts predictions through substring containment rather than normalized exact semantic labels, allowing ambiguous or contradictory answers to score as correct.

A provider is classified unavailable (UNHEALTHY / RATE_LIMITED / OFFLINE) because a health probe used a stale, invented, duplicated, or non-authoritative endpoint instead of resolving the provider endpoint from canonical configuration.
examples: health probe used http://localhost:9966 while canonical NINEROUTER_URL resolves http://127.0.0.1:20128
benchmark script hardcodes a port that differs from the configured gateway
required_reaction: RESOLVE ENDPOINT ONLY FROM: explicit env config -> canonical 9Router config -> provider registry -> installation discovery

patterns.definition: A dataset is called balanced while individual evaluated dimensions remain strongly majority-dominated (e.g. an 88% majority baseline for a binary property), letting an always-majority predictor appear competent without demonstrating discrimination.
required_reaction: COMPUTE PER-PROPERTY CLASS DISTRIBUTIONS BEFORE MODEL RUN
RECORD TRIVIAL BASELINES (ALWAYS_MAJORITY / ALWAYS_NO / ALWAYS_CENTER / ALWAYS_DARK)

patterns.definition: A benchmark/tournament reports PASS despite having zero successful eligible evaluations because provider failures, HTTP errors, missing samples, or empty result sets are not included in its success predicate.
examples: visual critique: aggregate status=PASS while every model call returned HTTP 402
extraction: 10/10 HTTP 429 treated as quality=0% rather than PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE
embedding tournament: 0 successful embeddings counted as tournament completion
required_reaction: CORRECT AGGREGATOR TO REQUIRE MINIMUM SUCCESSFUL N
DO NOT CERTIFY ROLE FROM FAILED BENCHMARK

patterns.definition: A deliberately authored visual subject supplied by the Founder (concept creature / character / environment identity) is replaced by an easier generic geometric approximation (spheres/capsules/triangles, generic mascot body, palette + glowing eyes only).
examples: concept creature -> sphere/capsule composition
distinctive anatomy -> generic mascot body
character identity -> only palette + glowing eyes

patterns.definition: Assuming a 3D representation is higher fidelity merely because it is 3D. Medium (2D / 2.5D / hybrid / 3D) must be chosen from identity fidelity, visual quality, motion requirement, interaction requirement, and production maturity.
required_reaction: A HIGH-FIDELITY 2D CHARACTER BEATS A PRIMITIVE 3D APPROXIMATION

governing_principle: THE FOUNDATION MUST NEVER AGAIN TREAT: THE PLAN FOR A CAPABILITY AS: THE CAPABILITY.
